Perfume rating 4.14 out of 5 with 2,667 votes

Eau Rose by Diptyque is a Floral Fruity fragrance for women. Eau Rose was launched in 2012. Top notes are Litchi, Black Currant and Bergamot; middle notes are Rose, Geranium and Jasmine; base notes are Musk, White Honey and Virginia Cedar.

oli_k05 12/01/25 18:43

i love rose scents, but i felt i could never find one that smelled fun and cute until now. ive had le labo's rose, and it felt sad and heavy, so i wanted to stop wearing it in the warmer months. diptyque's rose is so uniquely fun, fresh, and cute that i've found myself still reaching for it at this point of the year even though i originally bought the bottle in the late spring/early summer. it has me smelling myself all day :D

Muddy Monsters 12/01/25 11:55

I received this as part of a Christmas discovery set that contained 5 perfumes from this line in travel sizes which are ideal for chucking inside your bag and going.
This is a simple, clean rose fragrance ideal for spring and summer days when you don't want to wear a fragrance that is loud and in your face - this is a relaxing fresh rose that is ideal for a day our or the office.
Longevity isn't amazing but I don't mind topping this up every now and again.
This smells like a gardenrose in the best possible way. All I nees is the tea dress to wear this with.


MSita 11/21/25 19:52

I wanted a pure, realistic rose. Out of the ones I tried, Eau Rose ended up being my favourite. I first sprayed it on a strip and left it in my car, and for days the scent kept catching my attention. I’m not even a big rose lover, but there’s something very natural and slightly sharp here that feels like a true rose.

It’s great for year round and I can't wait to layer it with Pivoine Suzhou or Delina La Roseé once the weather warms up.

silverlocusts 11/21/25 16:43

I much prefer the EDP version of Eau Rose, but the EDT is also really nice. Eau Rose EDT is fresh, springy, and a little sweet. Diptyque knows roses, so of course it is a stellar rose scent. While I do not think that this is a true soliflore, it is a very evocative fragrance. Imagine you're in a well-tended rose garden on a sunny spring morning, and you bend to smell a freshly opened bright pink rose bloom. You can smell the crisp air, the dewy grass surrounding, and the green, thorny stem, but the voluptuous bloom is the star of course. This is a perfect rose fragrance for the rose lover in either concentration, to be honest. A+ composition, no notes or critique at all. Silage and performance are not beastly by any means, but someone who would really enjoy it would probably not want it to be nuclear anyway. I could get 6-7 hours of noticeable scent just by dabbing the sample on the skin.

A fresh, green rather watery rose on the opening with an astringent ammonia note on the initial dry down on me which I think is the blackcurrant. A pleasant, inoffensive scent when it dries down properly, but when it comes to rose fragrances I prefer sweet, spicy, jammy ones like Phlur’s Rose Whip.

worldcat123 09/04/25 11:09

This perfume wears like a gently blooming rose. It's a rose floral throughout and the scent slowly opens up over time, starting bright then becoming sweeter as it warms to the skin. On first spray, I catch musk underpinning the rose. It's a rosy skin-scent. There's citrus, but just a tad, and some type of spicy-floral that weirdly reminds me of carnations. After an hour, it turns sort of soapy, in the dreamiest, rosiest way imaginable. (I think that's the geranium.) It's soapy in a way that ever so slightly reminds me of rose water. And then, it continues developing. I catch whiffs of honey and wonder where in the world the scent is coming from (spoiler: it's me). It's now rose with a honey chamomile tea-like quality. All throughout, it remains rosy, light, and airy. So dreamy and wonderful, the type of perfume I imagine Sleeping Beauty would wear. Of course, the longevity is terrible. At this price point, I would've preferred something with more lasting power. So this beauty, unfortunately, remains a "special occasions" scent only for me. That said, I may splurge on the solid perfume as well. It really is such a well-crafted fragrance.

morganbowden 09/02/25 17:33

Diptyque and I have a funny relationship in that we love each other but don’t get along all that well. Several times now, I’ve loved a scent - bought it and sprayed it - only for the smell to leave me an hour later. This is sadly not an exception but god it’s so lovely. Green, bright, juicy, all the things I love in a good rose — and yet at the same time, it’s not so fresh that it’s cold. This has a steamy quality to it, like getting out of a boiling hot shower and smothering warm skin in rose oil.
I’d actually pick this as an autumn/winter wear — maybe it will last longer on some knitwear.

Spring in a bottle! It is a very light, soft, and silky scent. Upon first application it smells like a garden of roses, sprigs of greenery, and has very floral/fruity mix. vanilque 08/05/25 13:23

Lately, I’ve come to the realization that rose is probably my favorite note in perfumery. so I’ve tried out different rose scents: Delina La Rosée, MFK’s À la Rose, Armani’s Pivoine Suzhou, and both the Eau Rose EDP and EDT. Ultimately, I decided to get this one.

This really does smell like a realistic, fresh, dewy rose. sparkly and soft too. I think it's truly beautiful.

KVE 05/25/25 15:26

I am a big time lover of rose perfumes, and I believe they all fall into one the following three types:

- English/garden rose which leans powdery, soapy or earthy. Not too sweet.Think Jo Malone Red Roses or Body Shop English Rose.
- ‘Damask’ rose perfumes. Often teamed with oud, it’s giving sexy, smokey, Morrocan market. Think Initio Atomic Rose.
- Finally, we have youthful, juicy rose which is where this perfume sits.

This is a sweet and happy perfume in large thanks to the lychee note at the top. It reminds me of a rose & lychee martini. It’s super moorish but the longevity is not great on this which given its price point is disappointing.

luvoxlixir 03/24/25 06:09

Eau Rose is the embodiment of a romantic, ethereal daydream. A soft cloud of florals suspended in light. It starts cool, dewy like morning—fresh, brisk, and almost sparkling, smallest hint of citrus zest dancing around the edges. The rose here I'd say is more a fairytale's rendering, soft and whispering, no dense, rich petals. Best described as a light, airy abstraction of the colour red, only one shrouded in delicate pale-pink transparency. Something of that nature.

The composition is an airy, seamless medley. Rose mingling with lychee, with that elegant sweet fruitiness, never too sweet. Aldehydes breathe life into it, offering that frosty, clean crispness that lifts the rose into something gorgeous, almost transparent. It’s not exactly a real rose, not in the thick, lush, velvety way some may expect. No, it’s something far more delicate, an idealized version—almost a rose by association rather than reality. It’s dreamy, like a memory of something you've never quite experienced.

Have I done it? After years of searching, have I finally found my perfect rose water perfume?!

Full disclosure, I love florals but I am very picky about florals. Synthetic smelling florals make me sick and give me a headache. When I was younger, I wore Chloe EDP as my daily scent and while not as synthetic as other rose scents I've tried it still gave me a headache. Now I absolutely adore the smell of roses. My grandmother, mother, and now myself were and are avid rose gardeners. The fresh scent of real roses floods me with joyful memories and I've yet to find a perfum that elicits those memories. Eau Rose is the closest I've gotten to capturing that scent memory. While the notes are somewhat similar to Chloe, the cedar note feels more present and the bergamot and black currant add a citrus / fruity note that leans aquatic on me. The result of that is on the nose this scent very much smells like a rose bush on a cooler day in Autumn after a fresh layer of mulch has been laid to prepare for winter. The rose is a natural rose and the bergamot and blackcurrant add a dewy, cool element while the cedar gives it a mulchy layer. All of these elements lend a sense of realism to the rose smell that is lacking in most rose scents I've tried. On dry down this softens into a lovely soft rose that loses the aquatic element but retains the mulch element from the cedar. So while it remains floral it never becomes one note but instead fades into a well rounded scent reminiscent of the last bush bloom before winter. It's a rose on a cold day sitting in mulch. Projection on first spray is moderate and after in hour projection is intimate but again Dipthyque has great longevity on my skin. I put this on before bed (very relaxing) and woke up 7 hrs later still very clearly able to smell this on myself. This scent is a very nice realistic take on the rose bush as a whole.

I am not a rose scent lover since it just smelled synthetic and too strong for my liking, and even Rose flowers I dislike. I tried Delina OG and the La Rosee one, which were both strong and too much for my nose to handle. I decluttered my Delina OG while I kept the La Rosee in hopes that I could learn to love her. Mustering up the courage, I tried Eau Rose EDT .

Eau Rose was a blind buy that I was scared that I'll regret, but was happy that I loved it! Looking at the top notes which are Litchi, Blackcurrant, and Bergamont, when I sprayed it on my skin, the first note that I spotted was the Blackcurrant. Then after some time, I got whiffs of the litchi, but somehow I did not detect the citrus from the bergamont.

If I were to compare this to another perfume, a close yet different fragrance that I adore as well, it would be Jo Malone Poppy and Barley. Since they both have Blackcurrant in their top notes.

Yes, it is rosey, I do smell the roses here, but it is not the jammy sweet type of rose like Delina, or the soapy fresh vibes of Chloe, or a spicy type of rose like Byredo Rose of no Man's Land. It is a beautiful, delicate, demure type of rose that uplifts your spirit.

Eau Rose is not overpowering, and is a crowd pleaser. I don't think anyone would hate this fragrance. But, if you were the type of person who wants a extraordinary and unique type of rose scent, I would not recommend this.

Yes it is a beautiful fragrance, but as it dries down, it does not transform or change that much. The longevity on my skin is around 3-4 hours and projects quite well during the first hour.

All in all, Eau Rose is definitely my top Rose Scent, with Rose Gourmand from Zara as second, and Deljna La Rosee as the third since those are my only rose focused scents.

It is a perfect summer or spring fragrance, and even as a signature scent. This would suit all ages.

RosaMilena 05/24/13 08:46

EAU ROSE by Diptyque

Breathtakingly beautiful Rose. Opens with a rush of bittersweet bergamot and juicy tart vine-ripe black currants followed immediately with a saturating flood of soft, tropical, delicately sweet litchi fruit. A pristinely fresh and glorious rose makes her entrance amongst the sparkling lemony threads of dewy-green geranium, which provides a zesty citric strength and additional support to the principal rose scent itself.

A subdued non-indolic jasmine woven throughout provides an extra touch of sweetly refined floral complexity without intruding on the precedence of the roses. A warm, clean cedar houses the entire creation beautifully, while a cozy white musk adds a delicate hint of tender sensuality. A fascinatingly delectable drop of honey infuses just a trace of voluptuously natural silken sweetness with complexity and depth.

The Rose here is poised gracefully between the refreshing cool vivid clarity of the Black Currant/Geranium, and the sumptuously smooth warm sweetness of the Litchi/Jasmine. The perfect balance achieved here between the pull of these four exceptionally contrasting elements, both of which are supportive of the Rose, yet diametrically opposed to each other, is what makes this composition a unique masterpiece. It is both simple and extremely refined. The myriad of subtle, elegant nuances woven within and throughout the strands of this scent tapestry succeed brilliantly.

This is exquisitely beautiful. Perhaps the most beautiful rose I have ever smelled on my skin. Sublime beauty personified in scent. I love this one completely and utterly.

I first tried this in Mecca about a week ago after sampling Á La Rose by Maison Francis Kurkdijan for the uptempth time and still not being sure about it (À La Rose, that is.)

I told the girls in Mecca that I was desperate to find a realistic smelling rose that was a sweet pink rose with no citrus and little to no woodiness in the base, since I hate anything that is strong or smells remotely masculine.

Well, they were right... this smells just like pure rosewater distilled from the rose! It delighted me so much, since the queen of flowers reigns supreme in this perfume and none of the other notes take over. All I can smell other than that is a tiny bit of litchi at the top to make it smell not as simple and a bit more sweet, but that's it. I also smell a tiny bit of the musk here, but I don't mind musk at all.

If you want a lovely and feminine smelling rose that smells like the floral and not disgusting potpourri, citrus or some woody masculine scent that would smell better on your boyfriend or husband, buy this! My search for the perfect rose scent is finally complete :)
